patch.value: The local preflight token-budget gate is red on a workstation and green in hosted CI for the same commit again, because the earlier remediation closed the one ambient channel that had bitten instead of closing the fixture's environment

Measured 2026-08-30 on e3897a319, the exact commit whose hosted ci.yml run 33302472322 is green.

pnpm quality:static fails locally. The failing assertion is repository-token-budget-required, and the single contributing violation is: health-default: 267 estimated tokens exceeds budget 164 tokens (health --check-only).

The measured output is host-dependent. Inside the gate's own fixture, pm health --check-only emits two warnings that no runner ever sees:
  provenance_resolver_zero_success:claude-code:model:claude_session_file:76
  provenance_resolver_zero_success:claude-code:version:claude_session_file:76
plus their two findings rows and an inflated projection block. Those rows are the whole overage.

Decisive control: node scripts/release/token-budget-gate.mjs fails when run inside an agent-harness session and passes on the identical tree when six further ambient variables are removed from the parent process environment (AI_AGENT, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID). Removing any one of the six alone is not sufficient; all six together are. The gate already neutralizes a 39-key descriptor-derived list for its child processes, and that list does include CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so the surviving channel is not the enumerated child environment. Reproducing the gate's exact child environment by hand against a one-item sandbox produces zero warnings, so the leak is not a property of a single CLI invocation either. The mechanism inside the fixture is not yet isolated and deliberately left to the implementer rather than guessed at here.

This is a recurrence, not a new class. pm-t7wn04 recorded the same sentence in July with a different ambient input: a gate red on a clean checkout of main and green in hosted CI for the same commit, because the measured output carried a telemetry warning whose presence depended on whether the local flush reached the network. Its acceptance criteria opened with the general property, that the measured surfaces are independent of ambient host state, and then immediately narrowed to a disjunction naming telemetry three times. The remediation followed the narrow clause. The general clause was never enforced, so the identical failure returned through the next ambient channel that happened to reach the fixture.

The second unenforced criterion is the one that would have caught this: a negative control proving the gate produces the same verdict on a runner and on a workstation for the same tree. No such control runs on a workstation carrying an agent harness, which is the configuration every agent-authored change is now produced under.

The cost is structural rather than cosmetic. Local preflight is the gate an agent runs before proposing a change, and it now fails for a reason the change did not cause, on every workstation running the harness that authors most of the changes. That trains exactly the behaviour the preflight exists to prevent, which is treating a red local gate as noise. It also means the token-budget baselines can only be regenerated by a runner, because --update on a workstation would bake harness-dependent rows into the committed baseline and turn hosted CI red.

The gate's fixture environment is closed rather than subtractive: the child processes run under an allowlisted environment containing only the variables the fixture declares it needs, so a host variable that no descriptor enumerates cannot reach a measured surface; The equivalence negative control that pm-t7wn04 specified actually runs, and it runs in the configuration that authors changes, meaning a workstation session carrying an agent-harness environment, so a workstation-versus-runner divergence fails the gate rather than being discovered by hand; Every measured surface whose content can vary with ambient host state is either excluded from the measurement with the exclusion declared, or is proven invariant by the equivalence control; A failing size verdict names the observed output that exceeded the budget rather than only the number, so the next divergence is diagnosable from the failure text alone; A negative control proves the equivalence check fails when a deliberately host-dependent row is introduced into a measured surface; The remediation is stated as the general property and not as a list of the specific ambient channels observed so far, and the assertion that enforces it is scoped to all measured surfaces rather than to the two channels that have now bitten

value.note: fixture env is subtractive not allowlisted; failure text now carries the observed output that exceeded the budget

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Partial remediation landed with this report: the gate's size verdicts now carry a bounded excerpt of the observed output, so the failure text names the rows that grew instead of only the number that grew. That is what turned this from an unexplained red gate into a diagnosis in one run, and it is the fourth acceptance criterion. The excerpt is held in memory on the measurement record only; budgetForMeasurement selects named fields, so nothing is persisted into scripts/release/token-budgets.json.

The remaining criteria are untouched and are the substance of this item: closing the fixture environment by allowlist, and actually running the workstation-versus-runner equivalence control that pm-t7wn04 specified and did not deliver.

Deliberately not done: regenerating the baseline with --update. On this workstation that would write harness-dependent rows into the committed manifest and turn hosted CI red, which is the exact inversion of the current failure and would make the gate agree with the workstation instead of making it independent of both.

value.note: verdict must match between a workstation harness session and a clean environment for the same tree
gate unit contract including the observed-output excerpt

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Second instance of this item's own failure mode, observed while landing the change that filed it.

pnpm quality:static passed locally at exit 0 and Gates (static) failed hosted, this time on ESLint. The cause is a different divergence from the ambient-state one this item describes: the local script pnpm quality:static does not include pnpm lint:eslint, while the hosted Gates (static) job runs both. So the command the contributing guide points at as the local equivalent of a hosted gate is a strict subset of it, and three lint errors reached main.

That belongs to this item's fourth and second acceptance criteria rather than to a new one: local and hosted invocations of every quality gate must be proven equivalent, or the divergence declared per gate with a reason. Today there is no such proof and no such declaration, so the divergence is discoverable only by pushing.

Recording both instances here so the remediation is scoped to the general property. The ambient-environment leak and the subset-command mismatch are two mechanisms for the same defect: a maintainer cannot learn from a local run what hosted CI will say.
